newsitem.title: FRANCE: French women's magazine launched with cover nude.
newsitem.headline: French women's magazine launched with cover nude.

text.p: A new monthly women's magazine arrived on French newsstands on Thursday with a tasteful nude photograph of a young French comic actress on its cover.

The magazine, DS, entering a market with well-established rivals like Cosmopolitain and Marie-Claire, aims to cover social issues as well as the classic beauty topics, editor Tina Kieffer says in an editorial.

On its cover Valerie Lemercier, perhaps best known for her role as a frumpy aristocrat who encounters her medieval ancestor in French time-travel comedy film Les Visiteurs, poses naked but in command, looking the camera in the eye.
High quality paper brings out striking photos, not only in the fashion section but also illustrating more serious topics.
Albanian women tout Kalashnikovs and a Malian nomadic tribeswoman is caught up in a desert storm across four colour pages near the beginning of the magazine.
There are articles on forced child labour in France and Britain and the pain endured by relatives of Belgium's paedophile victims.
And, more conventionally but more up-front than in most women's magazines, the stars reveal their secrets.
Valerie Lemercier speaks of her unease with doing a nude photo and Jack Nicholson confesses he used to be a lousy lay, but got in a lot of practice.
Kieffer, a television personality, says she wanted to produce a women's magazine with "sensitive and mature articles, fascinating accessible fashion and informed, not naive, beauty."
She also wanted "a journal of society which asks questions about trends, tracks problems, reflects changes and tackles news with our (women's) sensitivity, without compromise or fear."
With an unusually low 10 franc ($1.7) cover price, the magazine is not just targetting intellectuals, its spokeswoman said. "It is not aimed at an elite. It is aimed at all women," she said.
DS -- a play on the French word for goddess, "deesse" -- is financed by Jean-Yves Le Fur, a producer of videos in the fashion and modelling fields.
The new publication has to carve out its place in a market of some 30 French monthly women's magazines.

Its first issue drew in 20 pages of advertising plus a pull-out, with the usual selection of perfume, body and hair care, make-up, jewellery and clothing adverts, out of a total 132 pages and with a print-run of 200,000 copies.
Usually a first issue attracts about six pages of advertising, a spokeswoman for DS said.
